paper_a.title: A fast quantum mechanical algorithm for database search

paper_b.title: Strengths and Weaknesses of Quantum Computing

metadata.description: Matched pair of bounds for unstructured quantum search. Grover (paper A) gives the O(sqrt N) upper bound via an explicit iterative algorithm; BBBV (paper B) proves a matching Omega(sqrt N) lower bound via a hybrid argument and uses Grover's algorithm to certify the lower bound's tightness. Together they pin down the quantum query complexity of unstructured search up to constants, justifying a BI (bijection/equivalence-of-bounds) classification: paper B's lower-bound exponent and paper A's upper-bound exponent are the same number, and each paper explicitly cites the other to close the gap.

matches.explanation: Both define the unstructured single-marked-element search problem with oracle access. Grover frames it as identifying the unique S_nu among N=2^n states with C(S_nu)=1; BBBV frames it as distinguishing the empty oracle from one marking a single n-bit string y. Same mathematical problem in different oracle conventions (predicate C vs Boolean oracle A).

Direct cross-citation: BBBV's AP320.1 is explicitly the externally-cited Grover algorithm (origin_citation: 'Grover 1996'), i.e. paper A's AP319.1. Both describe the same iterative algorithm: alternate phase-inversion oracle queries with inversion-about-the-average for O(sqrt N) iterations. This is a paper-original (A) to external-citation (B) match — strong signal that B knows of and uses A's contribution.

Composite L2-vs-L1 entry (parent skipped on B side because BBBV cites Grover's algorithm without re-decomposing it into algorithm_step nodes). Paper A spells out the three steps — initialize uniform superposition, Grover iteration loop (phase inversion + diffusion), measure — while paper B summarises the entire algorithm as a single external citation. The decomposition itself is the meaningful difference.

Both papers describe the same operator that drives the search: paper A defines it as the diffusion transform D with D = -I + 2P (inversion about the average), and paper B describes the same step as the post-query state |psi_1(y)> = |psi_0> - (2/sqrt(2^n))|y>, which is exactly one phase-inversion + the resulting separation that the inversion-about-the-average will then amplify. Grover gives the matrix form; BBBV gives the wavefunction form.

Per-iteration amplitude growth. Paper A's Theorem 3 + equation EP319.2 give Delta k > 1/(2 sqrt N) per Grover iteration (linear amplitude growth in k, hence quadratic probability growth). Paper B's EP320.2 states the same fact in distance form: distance grows ~ 2k/sqrt(2^n), success probability ~ 4k^2/2^n. Same lemma, mirror notation.

Grover's main upper-bound theorem (O(sqrt N) queries, success probability > 1/2 after M < sqrt(2N) iterations) is exactly the result BBBV invokes when noting that 'Grover's algorithm matches' the 1/2 exponent (RP320.2). Paper-original (A) <-> external-citation+remark (B) match with the same numerical content.

Grover's Theorem 5 is an external citation of the BBBV lower bound Omega(sqrt N) — origin_citation 'Bennett, Bernstein, Brassard, Vazirani [BBBV96]'. Paper B's TP320.3 is the corresponding paper-original main result: NP not in BQTime(o(2^{n/2})) relative to a random oracle. Same theorem, opposite roles (external in A, paper-original in B). This is the strongest single piece of evidence that the two papers are bound to each other.

Both papers contain the meta-remark that the upper and lower bounds match up to constants. Grover's RP319.1 says the algorithm is within a small constant factor of optimal (combining TP319.4 and TP319.5); BBBV's RP320.2 says the 1/2 exponent in TP320.3 cannot be improved because Grover matches it. Symmetric observations of the same tightness fact.

Walsh-Hadamard transformation (origin: external in paper A; cited Deutsch-Jozsa). BBBV does not introduce or use the Walsh-Hadamard transform as a named object — it lives at a different level of abstraction (they work with general QTMs and oracle queries rather than spelling out the gate-level construction).

Selective phase rotation (paper-origin definition in A). The phase-flip oracle action is implicit in BBBV's EP320.1 but not separately defined. Listed as none because paper A treats it as a primitive of the construction while paper B abstracts it inside the oracle definition (DP320.1) without giving it a separate name.
Phase-Inversion Rotation Matrix R, used in paper A only as a building block of D = WRW. BBBV has no counterpart at this granularity.
Projection matrix P with P_{ij}=1/N. Auxiliary linear-algebra object internal to paper A's proof of D = -I + 2P; no counterpart in BBBV.

Local decomposition D = WRW. This is paper A's implementation theorem showing the diffusion transform factors into three local quantum operations. BBBV does not work at the gate level and so has no analogous factorization.
Proof of D = WRW (parent: TP319.1). Mirrors the unmatched parent theorem; included for completeness on Level-1 paper-origin proofs.

Action of diffusion on a two-level state (closed-form k_2, l_2 update). Paper A's amplitude-evolution lemma. BBBV only sketches the corresponding evolution at the level of EP320.1/EP320.2 without giving a paper-origin theorem; arguably analogous, but the granularity gap makes none the cleanest verdict.
Proof of TP319.2 (two-level amplitude update). No counterpart in BBBV.
Sign-preservation corollary under D. Internal monotonicity bookkeeping for paper A's induction. No counterpart in BBBV.
Proof of CP319.1. No counterpart in BBBV.
Probability conservation under D — explicit unitarity check. BBBV uses unitarity throughout (e.g. PSP320.4) but does not state a parallel corollary.
Proof of CP319.2. No counterpart in BBBV.
Proof of TP319.3 (Delta k > 1/(2 sqrt N)). The corresponding bound in BBBV (EP320.2) is asserted at the level of an equation rather than a derivation, so the proof itself has no paper-B analogue.
Oracle Quantum Turing Machine. BBBV's formal computational model; Grover works informally at the gate/state-vector level and does not introduce a TM-style oracle model.
Permutation oracle. Used in BBBV's NP intersect coNP separation; no counterpart in Grover.
BQTime^A complexity class. Grover does not work in the BQTime framework.
Query magnitude q_y. Specific to BBBV's hybrid argument; Grover never tracks per-string query magnitudes.
Tidy BQP machine. Subroutine-composition concept introduced by BBBV; no counterpart in Grover.
BBBV hybrid argument (flip-answers theorem). The technical heart of BBBV's lower bound; Grover has no lower-bound machinery and so no counterpart.
Few-strings-have-large-query-magnitude corollary. Lower-bound machinery; no Grover counterpart.
NP intersect coNP not in BQTime(o(2^{n/3})) relative to a random permutation oracle. BBBV-specific oracle separation; no counterpart in Grover.
Quantum one-way permutation existence relative to a random oracle. BBBV-specific cryptographic corollary.
BQP boosting / probability amplification. BBBV-specific construction (parallel with majority); Grover has no analogue.
Tidy-BQP / clean-output theorem. BBBV compute-copy-uncompute construction; no Grover counterpart.
BQP^BQP = BQP closure. BBBV-specific complexity-class result; no Grover counterpart.
Proof of TP320.2 (BBBV hybrid argument). No Grover counterpart since the parent theorem has none.
Proof of CP320.1. No Grover counterpart.
Proof of TP320.3 (NP not in BQTime(o(2^{n/2})) relative to random oracle). No Grover counterpart.
Proof of TP320.4. No Grover counterpart.
Proof of CP320.2. No Grover counterpart.
Proof of TP320.6 (BQP boosting). No Grover counterpart.
Proof of TP320.7 (Tidy BQP). No Grover counterpart.
Boosted majority-vote BQP machine algorithm. BBBV-specific QTM construction; no Grover counterpart.
Tidy-output (compute-copy-uncompute) algorithm. BBBV-specific subroutine construction; no Grover counterpart.
